title: The Chow immersion is a closed immersion and the pulled-back O(1) is relatively ample
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $g:Z\to S$ and $\pi:X'\to Z$ be proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $j:X'\to\mathbf P^m_S$ be an immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] into projective space over $S$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] with $p\circ j=g\circ\pi$, where $p:\mathbf P^m_S\to S$ is the structure morphism. Put $g'=g\circ\pi$ and $\mathcal L=j^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^m_S}(1)$ [def-pc-module-pullback], an invertible $\mathcal O_{X'}$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Then: (1) $j$ is a closed immersion, so $g'$ is projective [def-pc-projective-morphism]; (2) the induced morphism $(j,\pi):X'\to\mathbf P^m_S\times_SZ=\mathbf P^m_Z$ is a closed immersion, so $\pi$ is projective, and $\mathcal L\cong(j,\pi)^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^m_Z}(1)$; (3) for every affine open $V\subseteq S$ the restriction $\mathcal L|_{g'^{-1}(V)}$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], and for every affine open $W\subseteq Z$ the restriction $\mathcal L|_{\pi^{-1}(W)}$ is ample.

proof.text: Since $g$ and $\pi$ are proper, $g'=g\circ\pi=p\circ j$ is proper by the composition clause (a) of the permanence statement. The structure morphism $p:\mathbf P^m_S\to S$ is proper, hence separated by the definition of properness. So $j:X'\to\mathbf P^m_S$ is proper by the proper-over-separated lemma; being universally closed (base change along the identity), it has closed image. Since $j$ is an immersion with closed image, the immersion-with-closed-image criterion makes $j$ a closed immersion. As $g'$ is proper it is of finite type, in particular quasi-compact, and $g'=p\circ j$ with $j$ a closed immersion into $\mathbf P^m_S$; so $g'$ is projective by the definition of a projective morphism.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Proposition 30.19.1 (Tag 02O5), Chow paragraph; Remark 30.18.2 (Tag 0200), part (1)

proof.text: Since $j$ is a closed immersion over $S$, its base change along $g:Z\to S$ is a closed immersion $j\times\mathrm{id}_Z:X'\times_SZ\to\mathbf P^m_S\times_SZ=\mathbf P^m_Z$ (permanence (b); the identification $\mathbf P^m_S\times_SZ=Z\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^m_{\mathbf Z}=\mathbf P^m_Z$ is associativity of fibre products in the definition of $\mathbf P(n;-)$). The morphism $g$ is proper, hence separated, so its diagonal $\Delta_g:Z\to Z\times_SZ$ is a closed immersion. The graph $\Gamma_\pi=(\mathrm{id},\pi):X'\to X'\times_SZ$ is the base change of $\Delta_g$ along $\pi\times\mathrm{id}_Z:X'\times_SZ\to Z\times_SZ$ (elementary: $(X'\times_SZ)\times_{Z\times_SZ}Z\cong X'$ via $(x,z)$ with $\pi(x)=z$; Stacks, Schemes, semi-diagonal lemma), hence a closed immersion by permanence (b). The composite $(j\times\mathrm{id}_Z)\circ\Gamma_\pi$ is exactly $(j,\pi):X'\to\mathbf P^m_Z$. Both factors are closed immersions, hence proper by permanence (c) and immersions; so $(j,\pi)$ is proper by (a) and an immersion by (e), its image is closed (properness gives universal closedness), and it is a closed immersion by the immersion-with-closed-image criterion. Since $\pi$ is proper, it is quasi-compact, and $\pi$ is the composite of the closed immersion $(j,\pi)$ with the projection $\mathbf P^m_Z\to Z$; so $\pi$ is projective by definition. Finally $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^m_S}(1)$ and $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^m_Z}(1)$ are the pullbacks of $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^m_{\mathbf Z}}(1)$ along the projections to $\mathbf P^m_{\mathbf Z}$, and the projection $\mathbf P^m_Z\to\mathbf P^m_{\mathbf Z}$ composed with $(j,\pi)$ equals the projection $\mathbf P^m_S\to\mathbf P^m_{\mathbf Z}$ composed with $j$; by the composition compatibility of pullback, $(j,\pi)^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^m_Z}(1)\cong j^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^m_S}(1)=\mathcal L$.

source.place: Remark 30.18.2 (Tag 0200), part (1), and the base-change construction in the Chow paragraph of Proposition 30.19.1 (Tag 02O5)

proof.text: Let $V\subseteq S$ be an affine open, $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$. The base change of the closed immersion $j$ along the open immersion $V\to S$ is the restriction $j_V:g'^{-1}(V)\to p^{-1}(V)=V\times_S\mathbf P^m_S=\mathbf P^m_V$, a closed immersion by permanence (b), over $V$. By the composition compatibility of pullback, $j_V^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^m_V}(1)\cong\mathcal L|_{g'^{-1}(V)}$, both being pullbacks of $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^m_{\mathbf Z}}(1)$ along the same morphism $g'^{-1}(V)\to\mathbf P^m_{\mathbf Z}$. Applying the projective-ampleness statement to the closed immersion $j_V$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ shows that $\mathcal L|_{g'^{-1}(V)}$ is ample. This proves the asserted ampleness over affine opens of $S$.

Let $W\subseteq Z$ be an affine open. The base change of the closed immersion $(j,\pi)$ of step 2 along $W\to Z$ is a closed immersion $\pi^{-1}(W)=X'\times_ZW\to\mathbf P^m_Z\times_ZW=\mathbf P^m_W$ over $W$ (permanence (b)), and as in step 3 the pullback of $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^m_W}(1)$ along it is $\mathcal L|_{\pi^{-1}(W)}$ by step 2 and the composition compatibility of pullback. The same projective-ampleness statement over the affine base $W$ gives that $\mathcal L|_{\pi^{-1}(W)}$ is ample. Thus all three clauses of the item hold.
